details: The relay wrapper looks up extraKnownMarketplaces.relay, but the marketplace has been named amidman since 28 Oct, so it always falls back to ~/relay: on a machine where relay lives elsewhere the wrapper runs the wrong copy.
failing_case: Relay checked out at /opt/relay, `relay setup --global` run (user settings hold extraKnownMarketplaces.amidman.source.path = /opt/relay),
RELAY_ROOT unset, no ~/relay. A session's `relay ...` on PATH runs the wrapper: jq '.extraKnownMarketplaces.relay.source.path' is empty,
root = ~/relay, and it fails "relay: repository not found". Expected: it runs /opt/relay/bin/relay.
pass_cases: User settings with extraKnownMarketplaces.amidman.source.path = <dir with bin/relay>, RELAY_ROOT unset -> the wrapper execs <dir>/bin/relay.
RELAY_ROOT=<dir> set -> it uses RELAY_ROOT regardless of settings.
No settings file and ~/relay present -> falls back to ~/relay.
reason: tests/test_hook_bin_relay.py::WrapperLookup::test_settings_marketplace_path passes at head and fails at 4410a1727cba (empty stdout).
findings.summary: The relay wrapper looks up extraKnownMarketplaces.relay…

details: CONFIRMED by reading: the wrapper's key (plugins/front/bin/relay:9) and the test's settings key (line 122) are both literals; setup builds
the key from marketplace()[0]. The bug fixed here came from exactly this: the 28 Oct rename missed this one place (principle 6, the same
kind of failure: check_always_on() already exists for "a rename that missed one place"). Correct today, so LOW; cheap to close.
evidence: $ grep -n 'def marketplace' -A6 lib/relay_setup.py -> returns data["name"] from MARKETPLACE_FILE
failing_case: Rename the marketplace in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json from "amidman" to "x" (setup then writes extraKnownMarketplaces.x).
Today: WrapperLookup still writes settings under "amidman" and passes, while the real wrapper reads .amidman, finds nothing and falls
back to ~/relay: the same bug this change fixes, undetected. Expected: a test goes red, naming the wrapper.
fix_hint: In the test, read the name from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (json.load, key "name") and use it for the settings key; the wrapper may
stay a literal. Alternatively the wrapper reads the name with jq from "$root"-independent marketplace.json beside the plugin, but the
test-side tie is the smaller fix.
pass_cases: WrapperLookup.settings() writes the entry under the name read from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (lib/relay_setup.marketplace()[0]);
with the wrapper reading .amidman and marketplace.json named "amidman", the three WrapperLookup tests pass.
marketplace.json name changed to "x", wrapper unchanged -> test_settings_marketplace_path fails.
RELAY_ROOT set -> wrapper uses it regardless of settings (unchanged).
reason: tests/test_hook_bin_relay.py:122 settings key now read from marketplace.json; a rename turns the test red (fixer showed it with name x).
findings.summary: the wrapper and its test both hard-code the marketplace name amidman; a next rename in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json breaks the wrapper again with every test green
